from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite Review: The Concept of a Basis", [
            "A basis is our coordinate system.",
            "It defines the space grid.",
            "Coordinates are simple movement instructions."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Create basis vectors
        v1 = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=RIGHT, color="#FF0000")
        v2 = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=UP, color="#FF0000")
        self.place_at_grid(v1, 'C3')
        self.place_at_grid(v2, 'C3')
        v2.shift(UP * 0.8) # Simple alignment for demo
        
        self.play(Create(v1), Create(v2))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FF0000")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Show span of basis vectors covering the space
        grid_lines = VGroup()
        for i in range(-2, 3):
            line_v = Line(start=self.grid['A3']+UP*0.4, end=self.grid['F3']+UP*0.4, color="#00FF00")
            line_h = Line(start=self.grid['C1']+LEFT*0.4, end=self.grid['C6']+RIGHT*0.4, color="#00FF00")
            grid_lines.add(line_v, line_h)
        
        self.play(Create(grid_lines), run_time=2)
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00FF00")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Highlight linear independence (dot at origin/vectors)
        dot = Dot(color="#0000FF")
        self.place_at_grid(dot, 'C3')
        
        self.play(FadeIn(dot))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#0000FF")
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Problem: Changing the Perspective", 
                         ["Same point, different observers.", 
                          "Different grids change coordinates.", 
                          "The cat stays fixed."])
        
        # Grid A: Standard Square
        grid_a = Axes(x_range=[-2, 2], y_range=[-2, 2], x_length=4, y_length=4, axis_config={"include_numbers": False})
        grid_a.set_color("#FFFFFF")
        self.place_in_area(grid_a, 'A1', 'F6', scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # Grid B: Skewed
        grid_b = grid_a.copy()
        grid_b.set_color("#FFFF00")
        grid_b.apply_matrix([[1, 0.5], [0, 1]])
        
        cat = Dot(color="#FF00FF", radius=0.1)
        self.place_at_grid(cat, 'C3')
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(Create(grid_a), FadeIn(cat))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(Transform(grid_a, grid_b))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFFF00")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(Indicate(cat))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FF00FF")
        self.wait(1)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Use P for basis conversion.",
            "P translates between coordinate systems.",
            "Transformation happens through matrix multiplication.",
            "Old coordinates become new ones.",
            "System B maps to C."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Mechanism: The Change-of-Basis Matrix", lecture_lines)
        
        # Animation Elements
        matrix_p = MathTex("P = \\begin{pmatrix} a & b \\\\ c & d \\end{pmatrix}", color="#00FFFF")
        vector_v = MathTex("\\vec{v}_{old}", color="#FFFFFF")
        vector_new = MathTex("\\vec{v}_{new} = P \\vec{v}_{old}", color="#00FF00")

        self.place_at_grid(matrix_p, 'B2', scale_factor=1.2)
        self.place_at_grid(vector_v, 'D2', scale_factor=1.2)
        self.place_at_grid(vector_new, 'F2', scale_factor=1.2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(matrix_p))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#00FFFF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(vector_v))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFFFFF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(Write(vector_new))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#00FF00")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.wait(1)
        self.lecture[3].set_color("#FFFFFF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.wait(1)
        self.lecture[4].set_color("#00FFFF")

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Smart bases simplify complex problems.",
            "Operations look easier in diagonalization.",
            "Saves significant computation time.",
            "Spaceships need efficient physics calculations.",
            "Optimized basis enables faster physics."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Application: Why Do We Need This?", lecture_lines)
        
        # Elements
        rotation_obj = Square(side_length=1.5, color=WHITE).rotate(PI/6)
        calc_text = Text("Calculations", font_size=24, color=WHITE)
        efficiency_graph = VGroup(
            Line(ORIGIN, UP*1 + RIGHT*2),
            Line(ORIGIN, UP*2 + RIGHT*1)
        ).set_color(WHITE)
        
        self.place_at_grid(rotation_obj, "B2")
        self.place_at_grid(calc_text, "D2")
        self.place_in_area(efficiency_graph, "B4", "E6")
        
        self.add(rotation_obj, calc_text, efficiency_graph)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FF8800"), rotation_obj.animate.set_color("#FF8800"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#88FF00"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#0088FF"), efficiency_graph.animate.set_color("#0088FF"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(WHITE))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(WHITE))

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Summary & Synthesis", [
            "Basis defines our coordinate grid.",
            "Changing grids transforms coordinates.",
            "Matrices translate between these systems."
        ])
        
        # Visuals
        point = Dot(color=BLUE)
        label_world = Text("World Space", font_size=20, color=BLUE)
        label_local = Text("Local Space", font_size=20, color=YELLOW)
        arrow = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=RIGHT*1.5, color=WHITE)
        matrix_p = MathTex("P", color=WHITE)
        
        # Initial positions
        self.place_at_grid(point, "B2")
        self.place_at_grid(label_world, "B3")
        self.place_at_grid(arrow, "C3")
        self.place_at_grid(matrix_p, "C4")
        self.place_at_grid(label_local, "D3")
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))
        self.play(FadeIn(point), Write(label_world))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FF00FF"))
        self.play(GrowArrow(arrow), Write(matrix_p), FadeIn(label_local))
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: Change of Basis in Linear Algebra
outline.target_audience: Undergraduate students in Mathematics, Engineering, or Computer Science

sections.title: Prerequisite Review: The Concept of a Basis
sections.content: Define a basis as a 'coordinate system' (a set of linearly independent vectors that span the space). Visualize this as a grid: the standard basis {i, j} forms a square grid. Emphasize that coordinates are just 'instructions' on how many steps to take along these basis vectors.
sections.example: Represent a point (3, 2) on a standard graph paper; show the paths 3 steps right and 2 steps up.

sections.title: The Problem: Changing the Perspective
sections.content: Introduce the idea that the same physical point in space can be described by different observers using different grids. Show how changing the basis vectors stretches or rotates the grid, making the same coordinate represent a completely different location.
sections.example: A cat (the point) stands on a floor. Observer A uses a square grid; Observer B uses a skewed, diamond-shaped grid. The cat doesn't move, but its coordinate pair changes.

sections.title: The Mechanism: The Change-of-Basis Matrix
sections.content: Explain that to convert coordinates from basis B to basis C, we multiply by a transition matrix P. Graphically show the transformation process: Matrix P acts as a 'translator' between the two coordinate systems.
sections.example: An animation of a coordinate system rotating: the transition matrix P takes the 'old' coordinates and outputs the 'new' coordinates relative to the new, rotated grid.

sections.title: Application: Why Do We Need This?
sections.content: Explain that choosing a 'smart' basis can simplify complex problems. If a matrix represents a physical operation (like rotation or scaling), picking a basis where that operation looks simple (diagonalization) saves massive computation time.
sections.example: A game developer calculating the path of a spaceship. Using a basis aligned with the ship's current orientation makes physics calculations significantly easier than using the global world coordinate system.

sections.title: Summary & Synthesis
sections.content: Recap the flow: Basis → Change of Grid → Transition Matrix → Simplified Calculation. Ensure the audience understands that the 'Space' is invariant, while the 'Representation' is flexible.
sections.example: A summary graphic showing: [Point in World] --(Matrix P)--> [Point in Local Space]. Both represent the same location.
